gap.prompt: If she ___ about the delay, she would have waited.
gap.explain: Use past perfect in the third conditional.

gap.prompt: The manager insisted that every order ___ checked twice.
gap.explain: Use the subjunctive after insist that.

gap.prompt: Hardly ___ sat down when the phone rang.
He was accused ___ giving false information.
The new policy had a major ___ on productivity.
gap.explain: Impact is the noun; affect is a verb.

gap.prompt: I would rather you ___ the report today.
gap.explain: Use the past form after would rather you.

gap.prompt: Not only ___ the deadline, but he also reduced costs.
The contract is ___ to change without written agreement.
gap.explain: Unlikely is followed by to + infinitive.

mistake.sentence: Despite he was tired, he continued working.
mistake.explain: Use although, or despite being tired.

mistake.sentence: The number of customers have increased this year.
She suggested that he goes to the doctor.
mistake.explain: Use the base form after suggest that.

mistake.sentence: I am looking forward to hear from you.
mistake.explain: Use to hearing after look forward to.

mistake.sentence: He made me to repeat the instructions.
mistake.explain: After make someone, use the base verb.

mistake.sentence: If I would have known, I would have helped.
mistake.explain: Use had known in the if clause.

phrase.prompt: We need to ___ up with a solution before Friday.
phrase.explain: Come up with means produce an idea.

phrase.prompt: The company decided to ___ down operations in that region.
phrase.explain: Wind down means gradually reduce or close.

phrase.prompt: She managed to ___ round the strict rules.
phrase.explain: Get round means avoid a rule or problem.

phrase.prompt: The team must ___ up with the new schedule.
phrase.explain: Keep up with means stay at the same level.

phrase.prompt: They decided to ___ off the launch until May.
He was ___ up by the difficult questions.
phrase.explain: Be thrown up means be confused or surprised.

formation.prompt: The report highlighted several ___ in the process. (WEAK)
formation.explain: Use the plural noun form of weak.
Use the noun form of develop.

formation.prompt: He was ___ about the risks involved. (IGNORE)

dictation.sentence: If she had known about the delay, she would have waited.
The manager insisted that every order be checked twice.
Not only did he meet the deadline, but he also reduced costs.
The company decided to put off the launch until May.
The report highlighted several weaknesses in the process.
I would rather you finished the report today.
